text: The main function of bulliform cells in grasses is :
options: to make the leaf impermeable to fungal spores.
to minimize water loss during water stress.
solution: Correct Answer: Option (D) - to minimize water loss during water stress.. Bulliform cells are large, bubble-shaped epidermal cells present on the adaxial surface of grass leaves. During water stress, they lose water and become flaccid, causing the leaves to curl inward to minimize water loss.

text:

| :--- | :--- |
| A. Conjunctive tissue | I. Specialised cells in the vicinity of guard cells |
| B. Casparian strips | II. Endodermal cells rich in starch |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: Correct Answer: Option (C) - A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II. Conjunctive tissue is parenchymatous tissue situated between xylem and phloem in root (A-III); Casparian strips are suberin depositions on radial/tangential walls of endodermal cells (B-IV); Subsidiary cells are specialized epidermal cells neighboring guard cells (C-I); Starch sheath refers to the endodermis of dicot stems rich in starch grains (D-II).

text: Find the statement that is NOT correct with regard to the structure of monocot stem.
options: Vascular bundles are conjoint and closed.
solution: Correct Answer: Option (C) - Hypodermis is parenchymatous.. In monocot stems, the hypodermis is sclerenchymatous (providing mechanical support), not parenchymatous. Vascular bundles are conjoint, closed, and scattered in ground tissue; phloem parenchyma is absent.

text: Which of the following simple tissues are commonly found in the fruit walls of nuts and pulp of pear?
solution: Correct Answer: Option (A) - Sclereids. Sclereids (brachysclereids / stone cells) are extremely thick-walled, lignified, dead cells providing gritty texture in the pulp of pear, sapota, guava, and hard seed coats and fruit walls of nuts.

text: Which of the following helps in maintenance of the pressure gradient in sieve tubes?
solution: Correct Answer: Option (D) - Companion cells. Companion cells are specialized parenchymatous cells closely associated with sieve tube elements. They help maintain the pressure gradient in the sieve tubes.

text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In a dicotyledonous leaf, the adaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata than the abaxial epidermis. Statement II: In a dicotyledonous leaf, the adaxially placed palisade parenchyma is made up of elongated cells, which are arranged vertically and parallel to each other. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
solution: Correct Answer: Option (B) - Statement I is false but Statement II is true. In a dorsiventral (dicot) leaf, the abaxial (lower) epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial (upper) epidermis. Statement I is false. Palisade parenchyma consists of vertically elongated parallel cells placed towards the adaxial side. Statement II is true.

text: In the given figure, which component has thin outer walls and highly thickened inner walls?
solution: Correct Answer: Option (A) - C. In the stomatal apparatus, guard cells (labeled C/inner wall) have a thin, elastic outer wall and a highly thickened, inelastic inner wall facing the stomatal aperture.

text: Given below are two statements: Statement I : Parenchyma is living but collenchyma is dead tissue. Statement II : Gymnosperms lack xylem vessels but presence of xylem vessels is the characteristic of angiosperms. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: Correct Answer: Option (D) - Statement I is false but Statement II is true. Collenchyma is a living mechanical tissue composed of living cells with pectin thickenings at cell corners. Hence Statement I is false. Gymnosperms lack true xylem vessels (characteristic of angiosperms). Statement II is true.

text: Bulliform cells are responsible for
options: Inward curling of leaves in monocots.
Protecting the plant from salt stress.
Providing large spaces for storage of sugars.
solution: Correct Answer: Option (A) - Inward curling of leaves in monocots.. Bulliform cells on the adaxial epidermis of grass leaves become flaccid during water stress, leading to inward curling of leaves to reduce transpiration.

text: The transverse section of a plant part showed polyarch, radial and exarch xylem, with endodermis and pericycle. The plant part is identified as :
solution: Correct Answer: Option (A) - Monocot root. In monocot roots, the xylem bundles are polyarch (more than six), radial in arrangement, and exarch (protoxylem towards periphery).

text:
Consider the following plant tissues :

(A) Axillary buds
(B) Fascicular vascular cambium
(C) Interfascicular cambium
(D) Cork cambium
(E) Intercalary meristem

Identify the lateral meristems among the above.
solution: Correct Answer: Option (B) - (B), (C) and (D) only. Lateral meristems include fascicular vascular cambium (B), interfascicular cambium (C), and cork cambium/phellogen (D). Axillary buds and intercalary meristems are primary/apical derivatives.

text: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Endarch and exarch are the terms often used for describing the position of secondary xylem in the plant body. Statement II : Exarch condition is the most common feature of the root system. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
solution: Correct Answer: Option (C) - Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true. Endarch and exarch describe the relative position of protoxylem in primary xylem (not secondary xylem). Endarch occurs in stems and exarch occurs in roots. Statement I is false; Statement II is true.

text: Interfascicular cambium is present between
solution: Correct Answer: Option (D) - Two vascular bundles. Interfascicular cambium develops from cells of medullary rays situated between two adjacent vascular bundles in dicot stems.

text: The type of tissue commonly found in the fruit wall of nuts is :
solution: Correct Answer: Option (A) - Sclereid. Sclereids are found in the fruit walls of nuts, giving them mechanical strength.

text: Initiation of lateral roots and vascular cambium during secondary growth takes place in cells of
solution: Correct Answer: Option (A) - Pericycle. In dicot roots, both lateral roots and portions of the vascular cambium originate from cells of the pericycle.

text: Read the following statements about the vascular bundles: (a) In roots, xylem and phloem in a vascular bundle are arranged in an alternate manner along the different radii. (b) Conjoint closed vascular bundles do not possess cambium (c) In open vascular bundles, cambium is present in between xylem and phloem (d) The vascular bundles of dicotyledonous stem possess endarch protoxylem (e) In monocotyledonous root, usually there are more than six xylem bundles present Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: Correct Answer: Option (B) - (a), (b), (c), (d) and (e) only. All statements (a), (b), (c), (d), and (e) are correct descriptions of vascular bundles and plant anatomy.

text: Select the correct pair.

solution: Correct Answer: Option (A) - Bulliform cells.

text: The transverse section of a plant shows following anatomical features : (i) Large number of scattered vascular bundles surrounded by bundle sheath (ii) Large conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue (iii) Vascular bundles conjoint and closed (iv) Phloem parenchyma absent Identify the category of plant and its part:
solution: Correct Answer: Option (D) - Monocotyledonous stem. Scattered vascular bundles surrounded by bundle sheath, conjoint and closed vascular bundles, absence of phloem parenchyma, and parenchymatous ground tissue characterize monocotyledonous stem.

text: Regeneration of damaged growing grass following grazing is largely due to :
